item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-claim-audit/4","sentences":[{"id":"p1s1","status":"keep","reason":"The rental comparison is metaphorical and the ownership conclusion is argumentative; it adds no independently checkable external predicate.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s2","status":"keep","reason":"The device-purchase condition and maker's ability to disable features after sale are covered by c1 and c2.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is rhetorical commentary about the argument and adds no external factual premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts a general expectation about purchasers and ordinary safe and lawful use, which the request does not supply.","claims":[{"claim":"People who purchase something generally expect to decide how it behaves within ordinary limits of safe and lawful use.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What authoritative evidence establishes this general expectation among purchasers?"}]},{"id":"p2s2","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence presents possible contractual or usage arrangements as illustrative reasoning and does not report a real actor, practice, or prevalence.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The request supports post-sale feature disabling, but not the added premise that the feature vanishes because the maker changed its mind.","claims":[{"claim":"A device feature can work at one time and later disappear because the maker changes its mind.","kind":"bounded-fact","verification_question":"What documented example shows a maker removing a functioning device feature after sale because it changed its position?"}]},{"id":"p2s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a rhetorical question that adds no factual assertion.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s5","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes an unsupported assertion that the buyer owns the device only ceremonially and that the maker controls it whenever control matters.","claims":[{"claim":"In some device arrangements, the buyer's ownership is merely ceremonial while the maker retains control whenever control matters.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What authoritative evidence establishes that makers retain decisive control over devices in this general way?"}]},{"id":"p3s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative qualification about what should be required and contains no claim about what real makers currently do.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s2","status":"keep","reason":"The unsafe, defective, and incompatible cases are presented as hypothetical possibilities, while the remaining clause is normative.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The normative question includes unsupported factual premises that the buyer paid for the device and that the maker wants to retain remote control.","claims":[{"claim":"The buyer paid for the device.","kind":"bounded-fact","verification_question":"What transaction record establishes that the buyer paid for the device at issue?"},{"claim":"The maker wants to retain remote control over the device after sale.","kind":"bounded-fact","verification_question":"What authoritative statement or record shows that the maker wants to retain remote control after sale?"}]},{"id":"p3s4","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence is a logical comparison of powers and adds no independent external fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is an explicitly suggested imagined analogy.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s2","status":"keep","reason":"This continues the imagined house analogy and is not presented as a report about a real event.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is an unmistakably hypothetical builder scenario.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a reaction within the hypothetical scenario and adds no external predicate.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s5","status":"disclose","reason":"The metaphor is argumentative, but the assertion that the reader paid for the thing is an unsupported factual premise.","claims":[{"claim":"The reader paid for the device or object being discussed.","kind":"bounded-fact","verification_question":"What transaction record establishes that the reader paid for the device or object?"}]},{"id":"p5s1","status":"keep","reason":"The alleged reply is framed as an imagined opposing argument, not as an attributed real actor's statement.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is a conceptual distinction about the scope of an argument and does not report an external practice.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s3","status":"keep","reason":"The conclusion is a logical inference about authority after sale, with no additional external premise beyond the request-supported issue.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s4","status":"keep","reason":"The chair example is explicitly hypothetical.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is an evaluative argument and analogy, not an independently checkable factual report.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence generalizes about what technically curious readers will notice, which is a claim about reader behavior.","claims":[{"claim":"Technically curious readers will notice that software makes the boundary between ownership and maker control less visible.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence supports the claim about what technically curious readers notice?"}]},{"id":"p6s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes technical claims about how features may be implemented and exposed; the request supplies none of those details.","claims":[{"claim":"A device feature may be implemented in code, connected to a service, or exposed through an account.","kind":"bounded-fact","verification_question":"What technical documentation establishes these possible implementation and access mechanisms for the relevant device features?"}]},{"id":"p6s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts both that complexity leaves the user's interest intact and that it gives makers additional ways to exercise power without physical contact; the latter is an unsupported causal generalization.","claims":[{"claim":"Software complexity gives makers more ways to exercise control over device features without touching the physical device.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What technical or institutional evidence establishes that software complexity generally expands makers' ways to exercise such control?"}]},{"id":"p6s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative recommendation about how to evaluate engineering details.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s5","status":"keep","reason":"The question restates the request-supported possibility that a maker can technically disable a feature and adds no new external fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s6","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative question about entitlement after sale and adds no claim about current law or institutional practice.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s1","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence introduces the author's practical argument and does not assert a specific external fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s2","status":"disclose","reason":"It asserts a causal relationship between disappearing features and risk to the user's plans, which is not supplied by the request.","claims":[{"claim":"When a device feature can disappear, the user's plans inherit a risk the user did not choose.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that feature removal generally creates this unchosen risk for users' plans?"}]},{"id":"p7s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence generalizes about users learning workflows and depending on device behavior, and it asserts that products may contain silent feature-removal mechanisms.","claims":[{"claim":"Users may learn workflows or build habits that depend on a device's behavior before a feature disappears.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that users commonly develop such dependencies before feature removal?"},{"claim":"A product may include a silent mechanism that allows a depended-on feature to disappear.","kind":"bounded-fact","verification_question":"What documented product design demonstrates a silent mechanism for removing a feature users depend on?"}]},{"id":"p7s4","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts an unsupported causal account of how makers allocate risk and retain power to alter the bargain.","claims":[{"claim":"When a maker retains the power to change a device arrangement, it shifts the resulting risk onto the user while keeping that power.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes this general risk allocation and retained power by makers?"}]},{"id":"p7s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is an evaluative conclusion and contains no independent factual premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative proposal and does not claim that improvement, updates, or change are currently banned or permitted by any real institution.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is the requested normative rule about meaningful control over represented device features.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a proposed disclosure and consumer-choice rule, with no claim about existing law or company practice.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s4","status":"keep","reason":"The subscription comparison is metaphorical and argumentative, not a factual claim about a real product.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s5","status":"disclose","reason":"The normative warning adds unsupported causal and behavioral claims about what allowing feature removal will teach makers and how makers may act.","claims":[{"claim":"Treating every disappearing feature as ordinary will teach makers that they can revoke ownership whenever it suits them.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that public acceptance of disappearing features causes makers to adopt or perceive this power to revoke ownership?"}]},{"id":"p8s6","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative conclusion restating the proposed principle.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s7","status":"disclose","reason":"The permission-slip metaphor is argumentative, but the sentence also asserts that the reader paid for the arrangement, which the request does not supply.","claims":[{"claim":"The reader paid for the device or arrangement being discussed.","kind":"bounded-fact","verification_question":"What transaction record establishes that the reader paid for the device or arrangement?"}]}]}
